articles.description:
Suppose you add a todo validation test and also tidy another test in the same file. You stage only the new test. A commit message describing both edits would promise a change that is not in the commit.
Agent Toolbox includes Good Commit, a reusable instruction file that asks an AI coding assistant to inspect the Git index before proposing a message. Here is a reproducible example using its small JavaScript demo.
You need Git, Node.js to run the demo tests, and an assistant that can read files and run Git commands. No npm dependencies are required.
git clone https://github.com/zmo2s/agent-toolbox.git
cd agent-toolbox
git switch -c demo/partially-staged

Append this test to test/todo.test.js:
test("rejects an omitted title", () => {
  assert.throws(() => addTodo(), /Todo title is required/);…
articles.title: Write a commit message for what you staged, not everything you edited

Robot maps can contain thousands or millions of cells. Building one widget per cell is usually the wrong abstraction; use a rendering strategy that matches scale and update patterns.
Store dimensions, resolution, origin, and cells in a model. Apply deltas to the model and notify the renderer only when visible regions change.
CustomPainter can suit moderate grids with caching and repaint boundaries. Large, frequently changing maps may need tile caching or a native/GPU-backed renderer.
Batch cells into rows, tiles, or layers. Cache static geometry and invalidate changed regions where supported.
Robot pose may update often while occupancy maps change rarely. Render layers at appropriate cadences.

articles.author: vmodal_ai
articles.description:
Flutter + ROS 2: Correlating Traces Across UI, Gateway, and Robot


A slow dashboard can originate in the sensor, ROS 2 transport, gateway, network, decoder, state management, or rendering. Correlated traces make those bottlenecks distinguishable.
Carry a trace ID through gateway requests and robot-side events. For periodic telemetry, use a stream ID and sequence number.
Measure receive, decode, validation, state publication, and render scheduling separately. Message receipt is not the same as frame presentation.
Use monotonic durations within a process. Across hosts, synchronize clocks and record uncertainty, or compare independently measured segments.
Sample high-volume traces and avoid logging complete sensor payloads. Include enough metadata to reproduce behavior without exposing private media or location.
Replay representative traces and compare p95 stage duration, queue growth, stale-data frequency, and dropped messages.
This Dart snippet illustrates one part of the design. Adapt types, transport behavior, timestamp semantics, and platform APIs to your actual system before production use.
class TraceContext {
  const TraceContext({
    required this.traceId,
    required this.sequence,
    required this.stage,
  });
  final String traceId;
  final int sequence;
  final String stage;
}

Measure p95/p99 behavior on target hardware, not only a desktop simulator.
Bound queues and buffers; define what may be coalesced or dropped.
Keep heavy parsing, image processing, and inference away from the Flutter UI thread.
Track source timestamps, sequence numbers, stale-data rate, and dropped updates.
Test network degradation, reconnects, sustained operation, and resource pressure.
Keep control commands and critical alerts separate from replaceable telemetry.

When a camera or vision pipeline produces frames faster than the app can process them, a queue makes the interface increasingly delayed. A deliberate frame-skipping policy can improve responsiveness.
For preview or detection, the newest frame may matter more than every historical frame. Recording and safety-critical perception need different guarantees.
Keep at most one pending preview frame. If processing is busy, replace the pending preview frame rather than letting latency grow.
Inspect image format and buffer ownership. Convert formats only when needed, release buffers promptly, and consider native processing for device-specific camera pipelines.
